terms.proofCondition: At least $3,000 of settled cash received within 30 days, with no up-front capital.

strategy.title: Broker the twelve signed allergen-panel orders through Keystone Food Lab and collect $3,840 by day 12
strategy.why: Twelve snack makers signed orders at $320 per panel (EVIDENCE, Nov 21-27). Keystone Food Lab (ISO 17025) quoted $180 per panel in writing, results 5 business days from receipt, invoiced net 15. Samples reach the lab Dec 1, results Dec 8, makers pay within 2 days: $3,840 of settled cash by Dec 10 (day 12), above the $3,000 target. The lab is paid by Dec 23 (day 25), after the makers have paid, so no up-front capital is needed (exposure $0) and the margin is $140 per panel ($1,680 kept after the lab). Market volume is not a gap: the twelve buyers are already signed, so the parked buyerVolume question does not decide this plan.

reviews.reasons: EXECUTABLE is supported. Twelve snack makers signed orders at $320 per eight-allergen panel, payable on receipt of results (price fact EVIDENCE, twelve WRITTEN_ACCEPTANCE agreements); fulfilment is by the recorded fulfiller, Keystone Food Lab (ISO 17025, written quote $180/panel, 5 business days, net 15), so the lab is paid after the makers and exposure is $0 as the contract requires. Recomputed with Nov 28 = day 0: samples reach the lab Tue Dec 1 (day 3); 5 business days = Tue Dec 8 (day 10); makers pay within 2 days = Dec 10 (day 12); lab net 15 from results = Dec 23 (day 25). Settled cash 12 x $320 = $3,840 >= $3,000 by day 12 of 30; ten of the twelve would already reach $3,200, so two orders can fall away. Lab cost 12 x $180 = $2,160 paid day 25 from receipts; margin $1,680. Ledger matches the steps and the trace (collected $3,840 in window, max exposure $0, pre-proof spend $0). The parked buyerVolume question does not decide a plan whose buyers are signed.
findings: Recomputed: $3,840 settled by day 12; $2,160 lab bill paid day 25; $1,680 kept. The contract's metric is SETTLED_CASH received, which the plan meets; the owner should know the account holds $1,680 after the lab is paid.
Slack: 10 of 12 orders reach the target ($3,200), so the plan tolerates two non-payers.
Timing depends on the makers shipping samples Mon Nov 30 (day 2); a one-week slip still settles by ~day 19.
Operational note: ISSUE_AN_INVOICE is NOT_CONNECTED; invoicing on results (day 10) must be connected.

reviews.reasons: NO_PLAN is the right stance after the card changed. The opening's directCosts EVIDENCE fact now reads $340 per panel while its fulfillment EVIDENCE fact still cites Keystone's written quote of $180; two sourced figures for the same cost disagree, so the cost is contradicted and ECONOMICS is not established. Recomputed: at $180, 12 x ($320 - $180) = $1,680 margin and $3,840 settled by day 12; at $340, 12 x $340 = $4,080 owed to the lab against $3,840 collected, a $240 loss the owner would fund on day 25, which breaks cost-below-price and the $0 exposure limit. Which figure is right decides the plan, and the author names exactly that (decisiveLinks ECONOMICS, resolution: obtain Keystone's current itemised written quote). Not CONDITIONAL: a supplier quote is obtainable evidence, not an unknown only a live sales test measures. The earlier EXECUTABLE plan is correctly withdrawn; price, buyers, timing and fulfiller are otherwise unchanged.
findings: Recomputed both readings: $180 -> +$1,680 kept; $340 -> -$240 (12 x -$20). The gross settled cash ($3,840) would exceed the target either way, but a loss-making deal funded by the owner after collection is not inside a no-capital plan.
The decisive missing evidence is Keystone's current per-panel quote; resolution and research step are correct.
Minor: the NO_PLAN revision still lists a member with deals 10 and directCost null; harmless but inconsistent with a no-plan stance.
